text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000381 bills 99215 well above expectation, with nearly half on low-complexity patients, yet the small set of returned charts largely supports the billed level, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds in every complexity band, not just among sicker patients, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215s for routine presentations such as URI (J06.9 on C0214578, C0214627, C0214667), follow-up visits (Z09 on C0214961, C0216321) and UTI (N39.0 on C0215239, C0216666). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. Against this, the documented 99215 unsupported rate is below the comparison providers', and supported charts include low-complexity claims such as C0216480 (rash, no chronic conditions) documented as high MDM. This is why the case is ambiguous: either the visits were genuinely complex, or the notes are written to match the code. That second possibility cannot be dismissed, because the problems-flag rate is notable, some time entries repeat, a few notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test billed, and no audit trail was received to rule out cloned or templated notes. Reviewers should first pull additional charts for the low-complexity 99215s and compare them for templated MDM language and repeated times. They should also request the EHR audit trail to check note creation and copy-paste patterns before relying on the documentation match."}
